doc.title: Bill Berry and Buster Cooper interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Humor in music and Clark Terry
summary: People play their personalities; Clark Terry plays with lift and humor.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Talk to us about humor in the music.

Well that’s what it’s all about. And I think you know one of the greatest players to me is Clark Terry. And it always comes out of him, out of his instrument, you understand what I’m saying? But he plays cute. He plays with a little lift and a little thing.
He’s a happy guy. That’s his personality. And most people do play their personalities you know. So if you happen to be funny, and there are a lot of musicians who are very funny,
they’re good joke tellers, and funny things happen to us too. I mean things that I don’t think happen to others.
